CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to reassess the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to evaluate the effectiveness of the current medication regimen.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to the current treatment plan. He states that while his anxiety levels have remained stable since the last visit, the fluctuations in mood persist, leading to increased irritability and occasional difficulty in concentrating. He has been compliant with his sertraline at 300 mg daily, but he expresses concern regarding the ongoing impact of his symptoms on his work performance.
His tension-type headaches have shown slight improvement, now occurring three times a week, with an intensity rating averaging 5 out of 10. He continues to rely on ibuprofen for acute management but is cautious about long-term use due to previous gastrointestinal concerns. Mr. Smith has been maintaining a headache diary as recommended, which has helped him identify potential triggers related to stress and sleep disturbances.
Sleep quality has seen further improvement, with Mr. Smith now averaging 7 to 8 hours of sleep per night. He reports less morning grogginess, attributing this to the recent adjustment of trazodone to 75 mg at bedtime. However, he still experiences occasional difficulty falling asleep and has noted that his gabapentin, now at 200 mg nightly, may contribute to residual drowsiness.
Despite these improvements, persistent fatigue continues to be a significant issue, particularly during work hours. Mr. Smith describes episodes of exhaustion that hinder his productivity, leading him to consider adjustments in his work schedule to better accommodate his energy levels.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 100 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 9. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in physical activity, reporting that he has increased his lunchtime walks to 30 minutes. He maintains a diet rich in whole foods and continues to abstain from alcohol, with a deliberate effort to limit caffeine intake. He expresses a desire to explore relaxation techniques, such as mindfulness or yoga, to further manage his stress levels.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; mild irritability persists; sleep quality improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Headache frequency decreased; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears less fatigued than previous visit; mood appears anxious but cooperative. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; tenderness noted in the bilateral temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with mild distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Discuss potential adjunct therapies if symptoms persist, including consideration of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime; assess efficacy and side effects at the next follow-up. Gabapentin at 200 mg may be maintained, with close monitoring of morning drowsiness. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Increase topiramate to 150 mg daily to further reduce headache frequency and intensity. Continue headache diary for ongoing assessment. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Recommend continued lifestyle modifications including regular physical activity and stress management techniques. Consider referral for occupational therapy to address work-related fatigue.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-12-01 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain an open dialogue regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
